featured_reviews.name: Kevin Loilargosain
featured_reviews.review_text:
A fantastic and interactive Bollywood experience!

What a great experience! This tour is an absolute must if you're looking for an incredibly fun and interactive outing.

We started our day by dressing up in various iconic Bollywood outfits. We took pictures in these, which were then edited so professionally that it felt like we were in a real movie! After that, we hit the studio to sing our hearts out to famous Bollywood songs. As a great finale to this part, we even got to dance along with real Bollywood dancers.

Next, we were given a fascinating tour through the different studios. It was incredibly fun and special to get a peek at an active film set! After that, we were guided through the other studios and received engaging explanations about the whole process. This really brought the magic of filmmaking to life for us.

Finally, I want to give a huge compliment to the staff: everyone was incredibly friendly, enthusiastic, and helpful. They truly made this experience complete!

Film Studios: The Heart of Cinematic Magic

Film studios are the creative powerhouses that bring stories to life, turning scripts into immersive visual experiences. These spaces are more than just physical locations—they are hubs of imagination, where directors, actors, and technicians collaborate to craft films that captivate audiences worldwide. From grand soundstages to cutting-edge post-production facilities, film studios play a vital role in shaping the magic of cinema. Whether producing large-scale blockbusters or intimate indie films, these studios provide the foundation for storytelling at its finest, blending artistry with technical brilliance.

Yash Raj Films: A Legacy of Excellence in Indian Cinema

Yash Raj Films (YRF) stands as a pillar of Indian cinema, synonymous with grandeur, romance, and timeless storytelling. Founded by the visionary Yash Chopra, YRF has redefined Bollywood with its unparalleled craftsmanship, producing films that resonate across generations. From heartwarming love stories to gripping thrillers, the studio has consistently set new benchmarks in filmmaking. Beyond its artistic brilliance, YRF has also built an empire with its state-of-the-art studios, fostering talent and innovation. With its keen eye for storytelling and commitment to excellence, Yash Raj Films continues to shape the future of Indian cinema, leaving an indelible mark on audiences worldwide.

featured_reviews.name: Mesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
HIGHLIGHT - If you have been to Hyderabad's version, you will likely find this visit a complete letdown.

My recent visit to Mumbai Film City was far from what I had hoped. To start, the nearest metro station is Aarey, it is about 4 km away. From there, take an auto (no more than ₹150) straight to the official ticket counter. Be cautious, several individuals may try to sell you tickets along the way at inflated prices. Avoid them, as they are scammers.

After a long wait, we were taken inside the premises by an AC bus. Unfortunately, the experience was underwhelming from the beginning. Compared to Hyderabad's Film City, this one feels small, restricted, and poorly organized. Most of what you see are large tin sheets covering the sets, there is no access to the actual sets themselves. It felt like being shown billboards of what you could see, but never actually do.

The tour ends at Bollywood Park, which hosts a few staged performances. This was the only mildly enjoyable part. The on site restaurant is strictly vegetarian, which may not appeal to everyone, and the food was overpriced for its quality.

Overall, Mumbai Film City lacks substance, feels commercialized, and fails to deliver the behind the scenes magic one would expect. If you have been to Hyderabad's version, you will likely find this visit a complete letdown.

featured_reviews.name: Sachi Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Feedback – Indie Stay, Chembur

As a frequent traveler to Mumbai and someone who has stayed at various serviced apartments, I wish to bring the following points to the notice of fellow travelers while considering a stay at Indie Stay, Chembur.

Pros

- Excellent location with quick access to public transport.
- A café located right below the property serving good South Indian meals for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. The complimentary breakfast provided by the property has very limited options and is arranged from this café; it is better to step down and explore the wider variety of fresh, hot food available. One can also order directly, and the food is delivered to the room.
- Friendly and responsive staff who provide quick support.
- A safe and secure place, suitable for families.

Cons

- We were expecting a serviced apartment with basic kitchen facilities, as mentioned on their website. However, this property is not comparable to serviced apartments like Bombay House Company or similar setups that provide kitchen appliances, cookware, and crockery. Given the pricing, there are equally comfortable hotels in Chembur that may offer better value if an apartment-style stay is not essential.
- Despite booking directly with the property, we were surprised to find that they were overbooked. Initially, we were given a Cozy Room. Upon requesting the Urban Corner Room as per our booking, we were shifted to another room which appeared non-functional and possibly used as a makeshift staff room. The bed linen was torn, and it was evident that fresh sheets and covers had not been provided. The room did not have a working intercom, and the AC, though functional, was clearly in poor condition. Other basic accessories were provided only after repeated requests.
- We specifically required a serviced apartment where we could cook our own food. This property does not offer any cooking facilities, which was a significant drawback for us.
- There is absolutely no parking facility, as the property is located right at a busy crossroads. This was an oversight on our part while booking.
- Being located on a main road in Mumbai, traffic noise is constant—throughout the day, late into the night, and again early in the morning. Personally, we found this difficult to manage.
- The property does not have its own kitchen. Food listed on the in-house menu is arranged through a cloud kitchen. As a result, we preferred ordering via Swiggy as and when required.

Having said that, we booked this property after reading positive Google reviews. Unfortunately, our experience did not align with those reviews, and perhaps it simply wasn’t the right fit for us during this stay. Due diligence is definitely advised before booking.

featured_reviews.name: Vijay Desai
featured_reviews.review_text: First off, the location of this place on Google maps is wrong. It is inside the Film city, not outside. This is just the ticket office and where the bus picks you up. We were late but they were nice to call us and then wait for us. There were two half empty buses but no indication which one we should board. We boarded one only to find out later that it was the Hindi bus. So we asked for the buses to be stopped so we can transfer to the bus with English speaking guide. We spent in hour in the bus touring the Film city with only 2 stops. One was the famous temple that is reused in movies by changing Gods. They were getting it ready for a Shiva temple. That was interesting. Everything else was just drive by. Then they brought us to the "theme park" which had some interesting props and some shooting going on that we could watch. We saw Kadar Khan and few other actors. Then there was a very long (1-1/2 hr) live show which included dances by a SRK double. But we were basically made to watch rest of the mediocre show because the buses won't come to get you until the show is over. No one could ever tell us how long some activity is going to take which would have helped set expectations. The first 1 hour of actual tour is fun. Maybe 30 min in the theme park is sufficient. But rest of the 1-1/2 hrs of the talent show is just torture! Hardly anything was in English so we had to keep translating for our daughter who doesn't speak Hindi and also for several non Indians. All in all, kind of OK but could be better and more entertaining.

Dr. Jayantilal Gada, began his entrepreneurial journey, after passing 10th standard from the Gurukul Gujarati school in Ghatkopar in media and entertainment industry with a video library called Popular Video Cassette Company. He subsequently ventured into trading video rights and distributing video cassettes across India, soon becoming the largest video library not just in India but also in Asia.

In 1992, the business was restructured under the name ‘Popular Entertainment Network’ and began to acquire video rights for movies to be distributed over various mediums such as video cassettes, satellites, terrestrial platforms etc. The Company subsequently forayed into theatrical and distribution rights of movies.
